title: Adversarial finite-armed bandits with fixed feedback delay and limited tracking capacity
summary: Play one arm each round against a fixed loss sequence. Only tracked rounds deliver their selected-arm losses after a public fixed delay, and at most C outstanding rounds can be tracked.

description_paragraphs: Minimize the worst-case expected external regret against the best single fixed arm. The learner must act in every round; delayed feedback is conditional on tracking, not on whether an action was played.

model.instance: One fixed adversarial loss sequence and a public common delay.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: Every coordinate of each obliviously fixed loss vector belongs to $[0,1]$.

model.parameter_domain_description: Integers $K\ge2$, $T\ge1$, $1\le d<T$, $2\le C\le d+1$. The theorem window is specified separately.
model.interaction_timing: Play and decide tracking before current deliveries; deliveries happen at end of round.
model.adversary_information: The environment fixes the entire loss table before interaction and does not know the private seed.
description_paragraphs: Loss vectors are in $[0,1]^K$, fixed before play and independent of the learner seed. There is no sampling noise. The delay is fixed and known.

operations.query_signature: At $t$, play $a_t\in[K]$ and decide whether to track $t$.
operations.response_signature: At time $s+d$, return $(s,\ell_s(a_s))$ if $s$ was tracked.
operations.order_convention: Exact scalar loss; no derivative order.

feedback_quality.description: The exact loss at the arm played in the tracked round.

operations.coupling: All responses read one fixed loss table; untracked rounds and unselected arms are never observed.
operations.index_control: The learner chooses the action and tracking decision; the public fixed delay determines delivery.
operations.access_schedule: Deliveries at the end of the expiration round, after the current action and tracking decision.

auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.
oracle.query_domain_description: One selected arm per round plus a track-or-skip decision, subject to the outstanding cap.
description_paragraphs: Before play, an oblivious adversary fixes $(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T)$, with $\ell_t\in[0,1]^K$. The common delay $d$ is public.
At round $t$, choose and incur the loss of one arm $a_t\in[K]$, and decide whether to start tracking that round. These choices use earlier delivered feedback and private randomness.

At the end of round $t$, return $(s,\ell_s(a_s))$ for each still-tracked $s$ with $s+d=t$; release delivered slots. A round never tracked gives no feedback. No preemption is needed for the upper bound; this profile uses non-preemptive tracking.
At most $C$ rounds can be tracked at once, including a newly tracked round before that round's deliveries.

output.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
description_paragraphs: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.

metric.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
metric.finiteness_conditions: Both cumulative losses lie in [0,T], so their difference on each execution path lies in [-T,T].

components.description: At most C simultaneously tracked outstanding rounds.
Only an expiring tracked round supplies one selected-arm loss.

resource.budget_semantics: Fixed horizon and hard outstanding capacity cap on every execution path.

cost_rules.description: Tracking occupies one slot until delivery. A delivered tracked round contributes one scalar response.

resource.scalarization: Evaluate expected regret at fixed T and C; do not equate C with cumulative observed losses.
resource.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
resource.online_cost: One loss-incurring action per round. Track at most C outstanding indices.
resource.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
resource.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.
description_paragraphs: The profile measures regret at a fixed horizon and a fixed simultaneous tracking capacity. It does not bound internal arithmetic or total internal memory.

views.label: Causal randomized policies with non-preemptive tracking

algorithms.randomization: Private randomization allowed, independent of the fixed loss sequence.
algorithms.adaptivity: Any causal policy from the public data and feedback already delivered.
restrictions: Non-preemptive tracking. The cap C applies even before the end-of-round deliveries. No additional computational restriction.
algorithms.internal_computation: Exact internal processing and storage of already delivered losses are uncharged. Tracking slots refer to feedback acquisition, not ordinary internal memory.
description_paragraphs: All causal randomized learners and non-preemptive tracking policies satisfying the capacity cap are allowed. The lower bound also holds with preemption.

guarantees.complete_expression: The native objective is $\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{\ell_{1:T}}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: For a fixed loss table, take expectation over private randomness; then take worst case over fixed loss tables and optimize over admissible policies.
guarantees.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
guarantees.time_uniformity: The horizon T is fixed and public. The guarantee holds for that T; it does not automatically give an anytime result or a simultaneous high-probability statement for all T.
description_paragraphs: For each fixed admissible loss table, the upper bound controls $\mathbb E[R_T]$ over learner and tracking randomness. The lower bound concerns the worst fixed table for each allowed policy.

budget.description: T online rounds; at most C simultaneously tracked rounds on every execution path.

objects.definition: Loss vectors are in $[0,1]^K$, fixed before play and independent of the learner seed. There is no sampling noise. The delay is fixed and known.

norms.definition: The model specifies coordinate ranges of finite vectors. Discrete action labels have no derivative order. A placeholder norm imposes no additional geometric assumption.

At the end of round $t$, return $(s,\ell_s(a_s))$ for each still-tracked $s$ with $s+d=t$; release delivered slots. A round never tracked gives no feedback. No preemption is needed for the upper bound; this profile uses non-preemptive tracking.

protocols.adversary_information: The environment fixes the complete loss sequence before interaction. It may know the algorithm and public parameters but cannot depend on the learner's private seed. This is an oblivious environment; nonanticipation describes the learner's causal information and does not extend the specification to a history-adaptive adversary.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: Exactly one arm each round, even when its round is not tracked.
protocols.queries_per_round: One loss-incurring action and one optional tracking registration per round; at most one delivered loss per round for fixed delay.
protocols.past_requery: None. Delivered feedback can be processed; untracked past losses cannot be recovered.

evidence.supports: The witness uses batches of size $b=\max\{1,\lceil d/(C-1)\rceil\}$ and tracks one randomly chosen round per batch. The batch size enforces the capacity cap without preemption. The regret bound reduces to the displayed rate.

Every delivered feedback occupies one slot for $d+1$ rounds, so at most $\lfloor CT/(d+1)\rfloor$ feedback values are useful. The label-efficient bandit lower bound gives the capacity term, and the ordinary fixed-delay lower bound gives the delay term. The reduction permits even clairvoyant preemption.
